figures.finding: Since 10 October 2010 St Maarten is a country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands; the Kingdom reported that St Maarten enacted the transferred Antillean legislation, so the Netherlands Antilles' Labour Regulations 2000 and Youth Employment Decree, as reported below, are its starting rules (its own later changes not read).

value.follows: AN (Netherlands Antilles legislation transferred to and enacted by St Maarten)

sources.said: St Maarten enacted the transferred Antillean legislation
As a result, since 10 October 2010 the Kingdom has consisted of four rather than three countries of equal status: the Netherlands, Aruba, Curaçao and St Maarten.

De op het tijdstip van inwerkingtreding van deze Staatsregeling geldende landsverordeningen, landsbesluiten, houdende algemene maatregelen en andere besluiten van regelgevende aard van de Nederlandse Antillen, alsmede eilandsverordeningen en eilandsbesluiten, houdende algemene maatregelen, van het eilandgebied Sint Maarten blijven van kracht, totdat zij met inachtneming van de Staatsregeling zijn gewijzigd of ingetrokken.

figures.finding: Sint Maarten's labour ministry, on the Labour Regulation 2000 it kept in force, bars any work by children under fifteen, paid or not, with no exemption; children of twelve who have finished primary school may do work a Labour Decree names (apprenticeship, or undemanding work that is not dangerous, such as delivering newspapers); youthful persons of fifteen to eighteen may not do night work (19:00 to 07:00) or harmful work, save by exemption on a written petition to the Secretary General of the Ministry of Labour. Until 2026-11-03 this figure held the Kingdom's 2006 report on the Antillean rules: light work outside school hours, 07:00 to 19:00, a bar under sixteen in the Youth Employment Decree and exemptions from the Director of the Labour Affairs Department, which the ministry's own summary doesn't bear out.

value.lightWork: from 12 after primary school, only work a Labour Decree names (apprenticeship, or undemanding work that is not dangerous)

exemption.youthfulPersons: written petition to the Secretary General of the Ministry of Labour

sources.title: Ministry of Public Health, Social Development and Labor (Sint Maarten), Key Labor Law Highlights 8: Prohibition of child labour, night work/dangerous work for youthful persons and women (on the Labour Regulation 2000, P.B. 2000 no. 67)
sources.said: Children: Boys and girls who have not yet reached the age of 15 years ... It is prohibited to let children work, whether or not in exchange for wages of compensation. ... Furthermore, children who have reached the age of 12 and who have graduated from the primary elementary school, may perform certain work to be stated in a Labour Decree, as long as these activities: a. are necessary for the learning of a trade or profession (“apprenticeship”); b. do not require physically or mentally high standards and may not be of a dangerous nature (e.g. newspaper delivery). ... It is prohibited for children and youthful persons to perform night work, whether or not in exchange for wages or compensation. By night it is meant: the time between 7.00 p.m. and 7.00 a.m. ... Articles 2 – 26 of the Labour Decree for Youthful Persons does not apply, if the work is performed by a youthful person of 16 years or older under the guidance of an expert in connection approved vocational training. ... Children No exemption is possible of the prohibition of child labour. Youthful persons For certain cases there is a possibility under the Labour Decree for Youthful Persons to get an exemption from the prohibitions mentioned in the Decree. A written petition has to be presented to the Secretary General of the Ministry of Labour.
